source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: PDF p.17 (taxable IRAs, pensions and annuities are income); no age-based amount printed anywhere in the booklet; PDF p.16 Line 22; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 90,000.00 + employer plan distribution (person 1) 30,000.00 = 120,000.00. Federal taxable income = 120,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = 85,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 85,300.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 85,300.00. Subtractions lines 5-16: none; line 17 = 0.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 85,300.00 - 0.00 = 85,300.00. Line 19 = 85,300.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (85,300.00 - 80,975.00) = 1.95% x 4,325.00 = 84.3375, to the cent 84.34; the Tax Table row 85,300 to 85,350 gives 85; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: qualified income after lines 8 and 15 is 90,000.00 and 30,000.00; the lower is not more than 47,550.00, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 84.34. North Dakota has no age test, so nothing here turns on either person's age; the only age effect is the federal additional amount inside line 1b. IRA and employer plan distributions have no subtraction line.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
